protocol.question: Does group-aware post-processing improve held-out correctness probabilities beyond score-only calibration, and does this translate into better selective acceptance?
protocol.primary_comparison: multicalibration minus Platt, paired test Brier score
protocol.selection_metric: validation Brier score; ties prefer fewer patches
protocol.candidate_policy: All ten recorded candidates, equally weighted within task. No best-of-ten selection. Alternate candidate j is paired with primary candidate j; index pairing is arbitrary, not a repair workflow.
protocol.split_policy: Preserve official validation and test partitions. Hash-sort official training task IDs, using the first 60% for base training and the rest for calibration. Never split sibling completions.
protocol.label: Publisher-provided is_correct from benchmark tests; not independently rerun and not a proof of semantic correctness.
protocol.feature_policy: Only prompt, generated program, and sampled-token log probabilities. No outcomes, difficulty annotations, task IDs, alternate-model features, or other candidate outcomes enter the confidence predictor.
protocol.cost_policy: User-selected relative cost scenario only. No measured dollars, latency, or Cursor deployment data.
protocol.scope: Independent offline replication and routing extension using public research data. No claim of a novel multicalibration algorithm, Cursor affiliation, or production validation. Protocol saved before this pipeline's test evaluation; not externally preregistered.

numerical_warnings: divide by zero encountered in matmul
provenance.numerical_check: Exported logistic probabilities match an independent non-BLAS einsum calculation to 1e-12 on every partition. All features and final probabilities are finite.

limitations: One benchmark and one frozen split; bootstrap intervals are conditional on the fitted models, not training-set uncertainty.
Publisher-provided labels and program extraction were not independently re-evaluated. Empty programs can encode extraction failures.
No private Cursor tasks, repository-level edits, live traffic, measured latency, or billing data.
Fixed groups and minimum task support do not establish population multicalibration guarantees. Worst-cell residuals are descriptive and selected across many cells.
Task IDs and exact prompts are disjoint; related problem families and pretraining contamination may still cross boundaries.
Alternate outputs are independent recorded solutions, not repairs. An alternate model can turn a passing primary answer into a failure.
Ten candidates are repeated trials, not a best-of-ten deployment. Feature extraction uses only the candidate being scored.
Examining test results and then revising this protocol makes future comparisons exploratory; a new final claim needs fresh held-out data.
